questions.text: PD 957 requires developers to allocate what percentage of a residential subdivision's gross area as open space?

rationale.a: 20% is not the standard; the requirement is 30%.
rationale.b: 25% is not the standard; the requirement is 30%.
rationale.c: PD 957 mandates 30% of the gross area be allocated to non-buildable open space, including parks, playgrounds, community facilities, and roads. This is reinforced by PD 1216.
rationale.d: 40% is higher than required; 30% is the correct threshold.
rationale.correct: PD 957 mandates 30% of the gross area be allocated to non-buildable open space, including parks, playgrounds, community facilities, and roads. This is reinforced by PD 1216.
rationale.takeaway: The 30% open space requirement is a core PD 957 provision tested frequently. This balances residential density with livability and ensures community facilities space.

questions.text: The Maceda Law (RA 6552) creates a critical threshold for installment buyer protections. At what point in the payment timeline do buyers become entitled to a 50% refund upon cancellation?

rationale.a: 1 year is below the threshold; no refund is due until 2 years.
rationale.b: RA 6552 establishes 2 years as the threshold. Buyers who paid less than 2 years receive only a grace period (no refund); buyers who paid 2 years or more receive 50% refund plus 5% per year above 5 years.
rationale.c: 3 years earns 50% refund (same as 2 years), but 2 years is the threshold.
rationale.d: 5 years earns higher than 50% refund due to the 5% per year add-on, but the base refund applies at 2 years.
rationale.correct: RA 6552 establishes 2 years as the threshold. Buyers who paid less than 2 years receive only a grace period (no refund); buyers who paid 2 years or more receive 50% refund plus 5% per year above 5 years.
rationale.takeaway: The 2-year threshold is the most frequently tested Maceda Law provision. Students often forget the threshold or confuse it with the 5-year add-on rule. Memorize: <2 yrs = grace only; ≥2 yrs = 50% refund.

questions.text: Under RA 7279, within what distance of an estero (drainage canal) are informal settlers considered to occupy a danger area where relocation may be waived?

rationale.a: 1 meter is too narrow; the statutory threshold is 3 meters.
rationale.b: RA 7279 designates areas within 3 meters of esteros as danger zones where occupants may be evicted without permanent resettlement being required first (though 30-day notice is still required).
rationale.c: 5 meters is broader than the statutory requirement; 3 meters is correct.
rationale.d: 10 meters is significantly broader than required; 3 meters is the law.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 designates areas within 3 meters of esteros as danger zones where occupants may be evicted without permanent resettlement being required first. However, 30-day written notice and a court order (Writ of Demolition) remain mandatory even in danger zones.
rationale.takeaway: RA 7279 danger areas are: 3m from esteros AND 50m from railroad. These specific distances are frequently tested together. Note that 30-day notice still applies even in danger areas.

questions.text: Under RA 10884 (Balanced Housing Development Program), developers of open-market housing projects must produce socialized housing equivalent to what percentage of the project cost?

rationale.a: 5–10% is below the statutory requirement; RA 10884 specifies 15–20%.
rationale.b: 10–15% is below the statutory requirement; RA 10884 specifies 15–20%.
rationale.c: RA 10884 quantified the balanced housing requirement as 15–20% of the project cost. This updated the original RA 7279 mandate with specific percentages to ensure developers meet the social obligation.
rationale.d: 20–25% exceeds the statutory range; RA 10884 caps it at 20%.
rationale.correct: RA 10884 quantified the balanced housing requirement as 15–20% of the project cost. This updated the original RA 7279 mandate with specific percentages to ensure developers meet the social obligation.
rationale.takeaway: RA 10884 (2016) is the modern enforcement tool for balanced housing. It quantifies the requirement in specific percentages, making enforcement measurable. The range is 15–20%, not a fixed rate.

questions.text: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for socialized housing single detached units?

rationale.a: BP 220, as amended (HLURB Res. No. 824, Series of 2008, Table 7), specifies a minimum lot area of 64 sq.m. for socialized housing single detached units. This applies regardless of whether the development is a new subdivision or an infill project.
rationale.b: 72 sq.m. is the minimum lot area for economic housing single detached units, not socialized.
rationale.c: 28 sq.m. is the minimum lot area for socialized row houses, not single detached units.
rationale.d: 48 sq.m. is the minimum lot area for socialized duplex or single attached units, not single detached.
rationale.correct: BP 220, as amended (HLURB Res. No. 824, Series of 2008, Table 7), specifies a minimum lot area of 64 sq.m. for socialized housing single detached units. This applies regardless of whether the development is a new subdivision or an infill project.
rationale.takeaway: The minimum lot area for socialized housing depends on the housing type, not on whether it is infill or new subdivision. Single detached socialized units require 64 sq.m. This distinction is frequently tested.

questions.text: Which law establishes the minimum lot area standards for socialized and economic housing in the Philippines?

options.text: PD 957 (Subdivision and Condominium Buyers Protective Decree)

rationale.a: PD 957 governs market-rate subdivisions and condominiums, not area standards for socialized or economic housing.
rationale.b: BP 220 is the law that specifies minimum lot areas for socialized and economic housing, covering both new subdivisions and infill projects.
rationale.c: RA 7279 (UDHA) governs eviction protections and balanced housing percentage, not minimum lot areas.
rationale.d: RA 6552 (Maceda Law) governs installment buyer protections and grace periods, not lot areas.
rationale.correct: BP 220, as amended, specifies minimum lot areas: for socialized housing — 64 sq.m. (single detached), 48 sq.m. (duplex/single attached), 28 sq.m. (row house); for economic housing — 72 sq.m. (single detached), 54 sq.m. (duplex/single attached), 36 sq.m. (row house).
rationale.takeaway: Always distinguish between PD 957 (market-rate regulation) and BP 220 (minimum standards for affordable housing). This is the highest-frequency error in housing law content.

questions.text: A developer plans a 500-hectare open-market residential subdivision. The project will be built in three phases over 10 years. According to PD 957 and PD 1216, what total area must be allocated as non-buildable open space across the entire project?

rationale.a: 10% is too low; the requirement is 30% of the gross area.
rationale.b: 20% is below the 30% threshold mandated by law.
rationale.c: PD 957 and PD 1216 both mandate 30% of the gross area as non-buildable open space. 30% of 500 hectares = 150 hectares. The phased development does not change the total requirement.
rationale.d: 40% exceeds the legal requirement; 30% is the maximum allowed reduction from buildable area.
rationale.correct: PD 957 and PD 1216 both mandate 30% of the gross area as non-buildable open space. 30% of 500 hectares = 150 hectares. The phased development does not change the total requirement.
rationale.takeaway: The 30% open space calculation is straightforward: Gross Area × 0.30 = Open Space Requirement. Students must apply this to realistic project sizes. The phasing does not alter the total obligation.

questions.text: A buyer has paid 4 years of installments on a subdivision lot and then defaults on a payment. According to the Maceda Law, how many months of grace period is the buyer entitled to before the seller can cancel the contract?

rationale.a: 2 months would apply if 2 years were paid; this buyer paid 4 years.
rationale.b: 3 months would apply if 3 years were paid; this buyer paid 4 years.
rationale.c: RA 6552 provides a grace period of 1 month for every year of installments paid. A buyer with 4 years of payments is entitled to 4 months of grace after missing a payment.
rationale.d: 6 months exceeds the formula; only 1 month per year is allowed under RA 6552.
rationale.correct: RA 6552 provides a grace period of 1 month for every year of installments paid. A buyer with 4 years of payments is entitled to 4 months of grace after missing a payment.
rationale.takeaway: Grace period formula: 1 month per year paid. This allows buyers to catch up without losing their entire investment. It is tested with various payment durations — ensure students master the proportional calculation.

questions.text: An informal settler community occupies an area 2 meters from an estero. According to RA 7279, which of the following statements correctly describes the legal status of an eviction in this case?

options.text: The area is a danger zone, so eviction can proceed immediately without notice or resettlement, which disregards legal protections for informal settlers
The area is a danger zone, so the 30-day notice may be waived and resettlement is not required, but the eviction must still be court-ordered.
The area is not a danger zone because 2 meters is less than the 5-meter threshold under RA 7279, which misinterprets the law's application to danger zones
The area is a danger zone, but all three conditions (notice, court order, resettlement) must still be met before eviction is lawful, ensuring compliance with legal standards

rationale.a: Incorrect — Even in danger zones, a 30-day notice and court order are still required. Administrative demolition is illegal.
rationale.b: RA 7279 designates areas within 3 meters of esteros as danger zones. In danger zones, the requirement for certified resettlement is waived (immediate relocation to safety is allowed), but the 30-day notice and court order remain mandatory. The eviction must be formally ordered by the court.
rationale.c: Incorrect — RA 7279 specifies 3 meters, not 5 meters. At 2 meters, this is within the danger zone.
rationale.d: Incorrect — In danger zones, the resettlement requirement is waived (this is the whole point of designating danger areas). Notice and court order still apply.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 designates areas within 3 meters of esteros as danger zones. In danger zones, the requirement for certified resettlement is waived (immediate relocation to safety is allowed), but the 30-day notice and court order remain mandatory. The eviction must be formally ordered by the court.
rationale.takeaway: The danger zone provision is frequently misunderstood. Danger areas waive relocation, NOT notice or court process. All evictions remain subject to judicial oversight. The three-requirement rule is modified, not eliminated, in danger zones.

questions.text: According to RA 7279, a lawful eviction of informal settlers requires three simultaneous conditions. Which of the following is NOT one of the three required conditions?

options.text: 30-day written notice to occupants specifying the grounds for eviction and the proposed resettlement location
A court order (Writ of Demolition) issued by the proper judicial authority after due process proceedings
Certified adequate resettlement site available before eviction, verified by the local housing board as habitable
Compensation payment to occupants for improvements made

rationale.a: 30-day written notice IS one of the three required conditions.
rationale.b: Court order (Writ of Demolition) IS one of the three required conditions.
rationale.c: Certified adequate resettlement IS one of the three required conditions.
rationale.d: RA 7279 requires three conditions: (1) 30-day written notice, (2) court order, and (3) certified resettlement. Compensation for improvements is not a statutory requirement under RA 7279.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 requires three conditions: (1) 30-day written notice, (2) court order, and (3) certified resettlement. Compensation for improvements is not a statutory requirement under RA 7279.
rationale.takeaway: The three-requirement rule is the most heavily tested RA 7279 provision. All three must be satisfied or the eviction is illegal. Memorize: Notice + Court Order + Resettlement = lawful.
